source_spans.locator: JEP: General 115(1), published p.39, Abstract/opening: unified quantitative account; same multidimensional perceptual representation across the two task families; context-dependent dimension weighting; exemplar-memory and inferred-exemplar interpretations

JEP: General 115(1), published pp.40-41, Equations 1-6 and mapping discussion: item-confusion model, group-response rule, rejection of direct invariance, weighted multidimensional distance, scale and response-bias parameters, optimization working hypothesis

JEP: General 115(1), published pp.42-43, theoretical goals/method: static model at a given stable stage; two paid observers; 16 separable-dimension stimuli varying orthogonally in size and radial-line angle

JEP: General 115(1), published pp.43-44, procedure: extensive item-response practice and feedback; four group-assignment conditions; feedback-based learning phase; criterion over final 600 trials; subsequent transfer phase with unassigned stimuli

JEP: General 115(1), published pp.45-46, item-confusion scaling and group-response fits: perceptual coordinates derived from item-response confusion data and reused to predict group-response probabilities

JEP: General 115(1), published pp.46-49, simple versus augmented exemplar-memory fits: inferred assignment of previously unassigned stimuli improves fit, especially for criss-cross and interior-exterior structures
JEP: General 115(1), published pp.49-50, parameter analysis/Figure 10: fitted dimension weights differ across structures; optimization support strong for Subject 1 but mixed for Subject 2

JEP: General 115(1), published pp.50-51, memory-augmentation discussion: perceptual-confusability and repeated-transfer-decision accounts are proposed; experiment does not distinguish similarity-based from rule-based augmentation

JEP: General 115(1), published pp.53-54, General Discussion/Prospects for Generality: indirect mapping via context-dependent weighting; only two subjects, one 16-item stimulus set, and extensive prior experience limit generality

conditions: the same 16 perceptually confusable stimuli were used across item-specific and two-group response tasks; the stimuli varied orthogonally over four size levels and four radial-line-angle levels
the item-specific response phase included extensive prior practice and repeated feedback before the perceptual-coordinate solution was estimated
each group-assignment condition had a feedback-based acquisition phase followed by a transfer phase; eight stimuli were assigned during acquisition and eight were initially unassigned
four distinct group structures were tested: dimensional, criss-cross, interior-exterior, and diagonal
the quantitative account is explicitly static, intended for a given stable stage rather than as a model of the within-session acquisition trajectory
population: two paid adult observers, one male and one female; one observer was highly experienced in auditory psychophysical experiments
task: produce item-specific responses to a 16-member separable-dimension stimulus set under full- and single-dimension response conditions
learn two-group assignments with trial-by-trial and block-level feedback, then respond to both trained and initially unassigned stimuli during transfer
temporal_scope: item-specific response testing followed approximately 2,650 practice trials and included eight sessions plus additional sessions
group-assignment acquisition continued until performance exceeded chance on every trained exemplar over the final 600 trials of a session
transfer followed acquisition and repeatedly presented all 16 stimuli while withholding trial-level correctness feedback for the initially unassigned items
model parameters characterize relatively stable performance rather than the moment-by-moment acquisition process

nodes.description: 16-by-16 frequencies of item-specific stimulus-response confusions obtained under the full two-dimension response condition
two-dimensional psychological coordinates estimated from the item-confusion data and reused as the common base representation in later group-response fits
the particular assignment geometry relating trained stimuli to two response groups
repeated classification of eight assigned training exemplars with trial-by-trial correctness feedback and block-level performance summaries until the stated acquisition criterion was met
the eight experimenter-assigned training stimuli and their two-group assignments supplied during the acquisition phase
the eight remaining stimulus-set members introduced in transfer without experimentally specified correct group responses
model-fitted distribution of weight across the two component dimensions for a given response condition
model-fitted scale factor controlling overall discriminability of distances in the weighted perceptual space
pairwise confusability relation derived from weighted distances in the common perceptual-coordinate system
model-assumed set of remembered exemplars associated with each response group
augmented-model hypothesis that some initially unassigned stimuli become represented as members of one response group after experience
transfer phase presenting all 16 stimuli and recording two-group response frequencies, with correctness feedback retained only for trained exemplars
observed and model-predicted probabilities of assigning each stimulus to either response group
average percentage correct over the original training exemplars used to define the model's performance-optimal dimension weighting
above-chance performance for every trained exemplar over the final 600 trials of a learning session

relations.description: the item-confusion matrix is fitted to obtain the two-dimensional base coordinate representation reused in the later response model
the acquisition phase continues until the source-defined above-chance criterion is met on every trained exemplar over the final 600 trials
different group structures are associated with different fitted allocations of weight across the two component dimensions
the effective pair relation used by the model depends on the common coordinates, condition-specific dimension weights, and overall scale factor
two-group response probabilities are modeled from each probe item's weighted relation to exemplars represented in the two response-group memory sets
the transfer phase supplies the observed response proportions used to fit and evaluate the two-group response model
changing the fitted dimension weights systematically stretches or shrinks the effective space and therefore changes pairwise relations among stimuli

fitted weights lie near the model-defined optimum for most conditions of Subject 1 and for selected conditions of Subject 2, but the source explicitly reports nonoptimal cases and therefore does not support universal optimization

the augmented account proposes that repeated experience and prior choices for initially unassigned transfer items can add inferred exemplars to the remembered group sets; this is a model interpretation rather than a directly observed update rule
for some group structures, allowing inferred exemplars yields substantially better fits to transfer response probabilities than restricting memory to the experimenter-assigned training exemplars

the relation between item-specific and group-level performance is indirect: the same base coordinates are retained while condition-dependent dimension weighting changes the effective pair relations used to predict responses
